title: More Words Than Reality
targetDuration: 1–2 minutes; hard maximum 120 seconds after measured voice timing

scenes.title: The research looks finished
scenes.viewerPurpose: Impressive research artifacts need a separate question about evidence. Names a proposed Reality Gap between apparent research maturity and the work that survives relevant independent scrutiny.
scenes.composition: Place a polished manuscript, running code and favorable review around a researcher’s unresolved question. Use one strong scene title, flat uncluttered backgrounds, and enough quiet space for the current caption.
addOrChange: Place a polished manuscript, running code and favorable review around a researcher’s unresolved question.
Leave the evidence space beside the polished package visibly incomplete.

cues.text: The paper has equations, working code, and glowing reviews; what has it actually established?
cues.visualAction: Place a polished manuscript, running code and favorable review around a researcher’s unresolved question.
cues.emotion: Interested doubt; gently emphasize “actually established”. Let the sentence land in an ordinary speaking voice, with no dramatic swell.

cues.text: More Words Than Reality calls this the Reality Gap: research that looks mature before independent checks support it.
cues.visualAction: Leave the evidence space beside the polished package visibly incomplete.
cues.emotion: Clear and warmly interested; give a small emphasis to “Reality Gap”, then finish at an ordinary conversational pace without a dramatic rise.

scenes.title: What survived a check
scenes.viewerPurpose: One system can create both proposal and apparent confirmation. Many polished parts can inherit one error.

cues.text: That gives an old problem new force: impressive work can hide a shared mistake.
